prompt: How do I do a mail merge in Word?
completion:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** that works for the most recent versions of Microsoft Word (2016 / 2019 / 365) on Windows and Mac. If you’re using an older version the labels are slightly different, but the workflow is the same. --- ## 1. Prepare the data source | Option | How to create it | When to use it | |--------|------------------|----------------| | **Excel spreadsheet** | 1. Create a new Excel file.
2. In Row 1 put the column headers (e.g. *FirstName*, *LastName*, *Address*, *City*, *State*, *Zip*).
3. Fill the rows with the data for each recipient. | Most common; works with any recipient count. | | **Outlook contacts** | Use your Outlook address book. | If you already have the contacts in Outlook. | | **Word table** | Insert → Table → create a table with headers and rows. | When your data is small or you want to keep everything in Word. | | **Text file (.csv, .txt)** | Save a plain‑text file with comma‑separated values. | When you already have a .csv exported from somewhere. | > **Tip:** In Excel, format the sheet as a *Table* (`Insert > Table`). Word can only read the first table if you have multiple tables on the sheet. --- ## 2. Start the Mail Merge in Word ### 2.1 Launch the Mail Merge Wizard (optional but helpful) 1. **Word (Windows)** * Mailings > Start Mail Merge > Step by Step Mail Merge Wizard 2. **Word (Mac)** * Mailings > Start Mail Merge > Mail Merge Wizard This wizard walks you through the whole process. If you prefer a more manual approach, use the **Mailings** tab directly. --- ## 3. Set up the main document 1. **Choose the document type** * In the **Mailings** tab → Start Mail Merge → select *Letters*, *Envelopes*, *Email*, or *Labels*. * **Tip:** Pick *Letters* if you want a separate document for each recipient; *Email* lets you send messages directly from Word. 2. **Create a new document or use the current one** * **New** – Word opens a blank page. * **Current** – Word uses whatever text is already on the page. 3. **Insert a heading or any static text** (e.g., “Dear [FirstName], …”). * You can add this now or later. --- ## 4. Connect to your data source 1. **Mailings > Select Recipients > Use an Existing List** * Browse to your Excel file (or other source) and click **Open**. * If it’s Excel, you’ll see a dialog: choose the worksheet (and if you formatted as a Table, it will be selected automatically). * Word will now display a **Recipients** pane with all rows. 2. **Filter/Sort** (optional) * In the Recipients pane, click **Filter** or **Sort** to limit which records will be merged. --- ## 5. Insert Merge Fields 1. **Position the cursor** where you want personalized data. 2. **Mailings > Insert Merge Field** – choose a field from the list (e.g., *FirstName*, *Address*). 3. **Repeat** for every field you need. 4. **Preview** * Mailings > Preview Results (arrow icons). * Browse through records to ensure fields show the right data. **Example layout:** ``` [Greeting] Dear , We would like to invite you to...
, Best regards, [Your Name] ``` --- ## 6. Add an Address Block (if sending physical mail) 1. **Mailings > Address Block** 2. Choose **Standard** or **Block** formatting. 3. Word will automatically insert a merge field block that pulls *FirstName, LastName, Address, City, State, Zip*. --- ## 7. Finish the merge ### 7.1 For Printed Documents (Letters/Labels) 1. **Mailings > Finish & Merge** * **Edit Individual Documents** – creates a new Word document containing one page per recipient. * **Print Documents** – sends directly to the printer. * **Send Email Messages** – (skip if you’re printing). ### 7.2 For Email If you selected *Email* in step 3: 1. **Mailings > Finish & Merge > Send Email Messages** 2. In the dialog: * **To** – choose the field that holds the email address (e.g., *Email*). * **Subject line** – type your subject. * **Mail format** – choose **HTML** (recommended) or **Plain text**. 3. Click **OK** – Word will use Outlook to send each email. --- ## 8. Common Troubleshooting | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **Merge fields are showing as `«FieldName»` instead of data** | Make sure the data source is correctly connected. Click **Select Recipients > Use an Existing List** again and re‑select the sheet. | | **No rows show in the Recipients pane** | Your Excel file might have empty rows, a missing header row, or the table might not be recognized. Try formatting the Excel data as a Table (`Insert > Table`). | | **Wrong column appears in a field** | Double‑click the field in the document and delete it; re‑insert the correct field. | | **Blank lines in the output** | Check for empty cells in your data source; use a formula in Excel to fill blanks if needed. | | **Email merge fails** | Word uses Outlook. Ensure Outlook is set as the default mail client and that your email addresses are correct. | --- ## 9. Quick Reference Cheat Sheet | Action | Mailings tab button | |--------|---------------------| | Start Mail Merge | **Start Mail Merge** | | Choose recipients | **Select Recipients** | | Insert merge field | **Insert Merge Field** | | Preview results | **Preview Results** | | Finish & Merge | **Finish & Merge** | --- ## 10. Resources - **Microsoft Support – Mail Merge** https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/mail-merge-in-microsoft-word-0b6e6f58-8eb2-4c58-91fb-d3d8d1a2a6ee - **Video Tutorial (YouTube)** – “Word 365 Mail Merge for Beginners” (search online) --- ### A Practical Example Suppose you have a list of 50 customers and you want to send each a personalized thank‑you letter. 1. Create an Excel file with headers *FirstName, LastName, Email*. 2. In Word, start a new Letter. 3. Insert the merge fields: `Dear ,` followed by your message. 4. Click **Finish & Merge > Edit Individual Documents** – this gives you 50 pages. 5. Print or review, then send email via **Finish & Merge > Send Email Messages**. --- That’s it! Once you’ve gone through a few mail merges, the process will feel almost automatic. Happy merging!
